en: Salutations to Śrī Guhyakālī. Having washed one’s hands and feet and performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana), having entered the divine enclosure, having circumambulated [it], and having bowed to the Goddess with the five mudrās, one should then sit down.
Taking up the water vessel: *phreṃḥ astāya phaṭ*. Sprinkle the water: *phreṃ ṣhrīṃ (2) śogaṇa*.

*Phreṃ rhrīṃ* (2) [is] burning. *Phreṃ vhrīṃ* (2) [is] flooding. Having drawn a triangle, having written *vphreṃ* in its center: "We know Yogeśvarī; we meditate on Śrī Guhyakālī; may that Siddhi impel us. Thus, one sprinkles. Having consecrated [it] three times with *vphreṃ*, [one performs] the *dhenu-mudrā* and the *liṅga-mudrā*.

Having displayed the *yonimudrā*: *vphreṃ ātmatattvādhipati śrīguhyakāli ātmatattvaṃ śodhayāmi vphreṃ namaḥ svāhā vphreṃ* *vphreṃ vidyātattvādhipati śrīguhyakāli vidyātattvaṃ śodhayāmi vphreṃ namaḥ svāhā vphreṃ* *vphreṃ śivatattvādhipati*

O Śrī Guhyakālī, by means of the principle of Śiva (śivatatva), I purify; VPHREṂ NAMAḤ SVĀHĀ. VPHREṂ, O Sovereign of all principles (sarvatattvādhipati) Śrī Guhyakālī, I purify all principles; VPHREṂ NAMAḤ SVĀHĀ. Having thus performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana): VPHREṂ, the ritual sipping of water, beginning with the Maitra [mantras].
"Touching: *phaṭ* to the subtle [element]. Thus, having washed the hands and feet, one should also recite *vphreṃ*."

Having drawn a triangle in the middle of the hands and feet, having written *vphreṃ* on the hands and *vhrīṃ* on the feet, one should worship with *vprheṃ vhrīṃ*. [Then recite: *pheḥ astā phaṭ*! *phreḥ*! May those beings depart who are present here, those beings dwelling upon the earth, and those beings who are creators of obstacles!

"May they depart by the command of Śiva"—having thus scattered unbroken rice (*akṣata*) in the ten directions, and having performed the *phaḥ* for the expulsion [of obstacles] with three claps of the hands (*tāla*), saying "phaḥ! expel! haḍit!"—one should sprinkle the seat. Having drawn a triangle in the center of the seat and written "vphreṁ" in its center, [one should know that] for the mantra of the seat, Merupṛṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*) and Sutala is the meter (*chanda*).
The Kurma is the deity. This is the application in the worship of the seat (āsana-pūjā).
O Earth, you are supported by Viṣṇu in this world; as a goddess, you too are supported by him. Therefore, support me always and make my seat pure.

Phreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Kphreṃ, I worship the lotus-seated Śrīpādukā of all powers; I offer salutation, I satisfy with libation. Phreṃ Namaḥ Svāhā. [Thus] having worshipped the seat, one should display the Dhenu, Liṅga, and Yoni mudrās.
Then, having sat down, he should perform the formal declaration of intent (saṃkalpa).

Hphreṃ! For the sake of destroying all my sins, for the sake of pleasing Śrī Guhyakālī, and for the sake of virtue, wealth, desire, and liberation, I shall perform the sixteen-fold ritual service (*ṣoḍaśopacāra-pūjā*). Be pleased! Protect me! Protect me! Devour my enemies! Hūṃ Phaṭ! Namaḥ Svāhā!

*vphreṃ* to her who dwells in Caṇḍamuṇḍa, to Amṛtaguhyakālī, to Amṛtaśrīguhyabhairava—this is the water offering (*arghya*); *vphreṃ namaḥ svāhā*. Having thus presented the *arghya*, one should then worship Gaṇeśa with the mantra beginning "sumukhaśca" and so forth. Then: *śivādibhyaḥ śrīgurubhyo namaḥ*.

her matted locks like the waters of the ocean, she who bears the crescent moon as a digit of the moon’s descent.
I bow to that Bhāratī, who rests upon a lotus, whose hands hold an eye, a rosary, a jar, and a book, who is pure and of immeasurable form, and who bears the weight of full breasts and hips.

One should place [the syllables]: *a ā* (14), which pervade from the navel to the feet; *ka kha* (25), which precede the sin [of the body] and end with *ma*; and having performed the pervasive placement of *ya ra la va* etc., ending with *kṣa*. Then: *aphreṁ namaḥ* at the hairline; *āphreṁ namaḥ* on the circumference of the face.

*Ipheṃ namaḥ* to the right eye. *Īpheṃ namaḥ* to the left eye. *Upheṃ namaḥ* to the right ear. *Ūpheṃ namaḥ* to the left ear. *Ṛpheṃ namaḥ* to the right nostril. *Ṝpheṃ namaḥ* to the left nostril. *Ḷpheṃ namaḥ* to the right cheek. *Ḹpheṃ namaḥ* to the left cheek.
In the left ear: *ephreṃ* homage to the upper lip; *aiphreṃ* homage to the lower lip; *ophreṃ* homage to the upper lip; *auphreṃ* homage to the lower lip.

To the end of the feet. *Kṣphraṃ* *namaḥ* from the heart to the top of the head; one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*). Of this glorious Mantrayanara, Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chanda*), and Śrī Guhyakālī is the deity (*devatā*). (1) *Khphraṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *Kphraṃ* is the power (*śakti*), and *Kphraṃ* is the peg (*kīlaka*).

The application is for *prāṇāyāma*. [Perform] the *nyāsa* on the fingers and other limbs with *khphrāṃ*. Perform the *nyāsa* on the heart and other centers with the root *kuṭa*. Again, meditating upon the Goddess with the root mantra, utter *kphreṃ* eight times while exhaling the breath through the right nostril.

Again, reciting "khphreṁ" eight times, one should fill [the breath] with air through the right nostril. (1) Having bound both nostrils, one should hold the breath (kumbhaka) sixteen times while reciting the root mantra. Thus, at the end of the three [stages of] breath control (prāṇāyāma), [one recites]: "vphreṁ! Amṛtakarālī, the supreme light, rains down the nectar of primordial wisdom."
(2) *vphreṃ* namaḥ svāhā. By means of this mantra, one should cause the splendor residing in the root deity to descend onto the palm of one's own hand.

*vphreṃ sudhākarāli śrīguhyakāli vphreṃ namaḥ svāhā*. One should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*). Of this great mantra for the placement (*mahānyāsa*) of the liberation-in-life (*jīvanmukti*) of Śrī Kālī, Vāmadeva is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the *bṛhatī* is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Nirvāṇa-Śrī Guhyakālī is the deity.

Mahādevatā. (1) Bījaśakti is the second seed-power. Khphreṁ is the third power. Kphreṁ is the second power. Hskṣmlvryūṁ is the kīlaka. By the grace of Nirvāṇa Śrī Guhyakālī, preceded by liberation while living (jīvanmukti).

Siddhi Mahākāla Caṇḍayogeśvarī (2), Nirvāṇa Śrī Guhyakālī (1), namas svāhā. [At the base of the left fingers. Jvālājihvā Karālī Vaḍavānala Bhairavī (2), Nirvāṇa Śrī Guhyakālī (1), namas svāhā. [At the tip of the left foot. Mahāmudrā Karālī.

Siddhiyoginī (2), Nirvāṇa Śrīguhyakālī (1), namaḥ svāhā. On the right side: Ṛddhikarāli Mahāsiddhi Mahāyoginī (2), Śrīnirvāṇa Śrīguhyakālī (1), namaḥ svāhā. On the left side: Tuṣṭikarāli Kālasiddhi Caṇḍayoginī (2), Nirvāṇa...
Śrī Guhyakālī (1) Namaḥ Svāhā. [To be recited] at the navel.

(1) *Puṣṭikarāli Siddhimahācaṇḍayoginī* (2) *Nirvāṇa Śrīguhyakālī* (1) *Namaḥ Svāhā*. [Heart] (1) *Kaṅkālamālinī Siddhikālacaṇḍayoginī* (2) *Nirvāṇa Śrīguhyakālī* (1) *Namaḥ Svāhā*. [Right Breast] (1) *Mahārudrakarāli Siddhimahākālacaṇḍayoginī* (2) [Left Breast]

Nirvāṇa Śrī Guhyakālī (1), homage, svāhā! Kakudī (1). Sṛṣṭikarālī Brahmakālī (2), Nirvāṇa Śrī Guhyakālī (1), homage, svāhā! On the left breast (1). Sthitikarālī Viṣṇukālī (2), Nirvāṇa Śrī Guhyakālī (1), homage, svāhā! From the right breast...

From the right breast down to the fingers of the right hand: *saṃhārakāli rudrakāli* (2), *nirvāṇaśrīguhyakāli* (1), *namaḥ svāhā*. From the left breast down to the fingers of the left hand: *(1)* *anākhyākarāli maheśvarakāli*.

(2) *Nirvāṇa-śrī-guhyakālī* (1) *namaḥ svāhā*. From the navel to the tips of the toes of the right foot: (1) *Bhāsākālī*, *Sadāśivakālī*, (2) *Nirvāṇa-śrī-guhyakālī* (1) *namaḥ svāhā*. From the navel to the end of the left foot: (1) *Madānādahūṃkālī*, *Karālī*.

*Jayamaṅgalākālī* (2), *Nirvāṇaśrīguhyakālī* (1), *Namaḥ svāhā*. From the head to the feet: (1) *Namaḥ svāhā* to the limit of *Nirvāṇaśrīguhyakālī*, who is distinct from the three states and the three bodies. (1)

I am the venerable Guhyakālī, who is liberated while living, eternally pure, awakened, free, completely full, true, supreme, infinite bliss, and the Nirvāṇa of the Supreme Brahman; I alone am the Nirvāṇa, the venerable Guhyakālī. I consider myself to have become the subduer; everything is established in me, and everything goes to its dissolution in me. Therefore...

*Sad-brahma-viṣṇu-guhyakāli (1) namaḥ svāhā*. Having touched the heart with this, one should recite it. One should perform the root-assignment (*mūla-nyāsa*). Of this glorious *Nirvāṇa-śrī-guhyakālī* great mantra, Vaḍavānala is the seer (*ṛṣi*) and the unformed (*akṛti*) is the meter (*chandaḥ*).
The deity Śrī Guhyakālī is Nirvāṇa. Oṃ is the seed syllable; Hphreṃ is the power (śakti); Kphreṃ is the wedge (kīlaka).

This is the application (*viniyoga*) for the placement and worship (*nyāsapūjā*) for the purpose of attaining proximity to Nirvāṇa-Śrī-Guhyakālī, preceded by grace through the gateway, for the sake of accomplishing dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa.

Hphraṃ: The finger-placement (aṅganyāsa) and so forth. Kphreṃ sarvajñe śaktidhāmni nirvāṇa śrīguhyakāli hphreṃ namaḥ svāhā | To the heart, namaḥ. Kphreṃ anityatṛptiśaktidhāmni nirvāṇa śrīguhyakāli hphreṃ namaḥ svāhā | To the head.

Svāhā! Hphreṃ! To Nirvāṇa Śrī Guhyakālī, the abode of the power of primordial awakening, Hphreṃ! Homage, Svāhā! To the head, Vauṣaṭ! Hphreṃ! To Nirvāṇa Śrī Guhyakālī, the abode of the independent power, Hphreṃ! Homage, Svāhā! To the armor, Hūṃ!
Phreṃ, obeisance and svāhā to the glorious Guhyakālī, O Nirvāṇa, whose abode is the power that is never lost! Phreṃ namaḥ svāhā.

To the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*. *Hphreṃ*, obeisance and *svāhā* to the Nirvāṇa Śrī Guhyakālī, the abode of infinite power, *hphreṃ*! To the weapon, *phaṭ*. [This is] the meditation on the form of the root-mantra. Now follows the installation of the water-pot (*kalaśa*).

Having drawn a triangle, a ten-petalled lotus, and a square on the ground: *Phreṃ Śrī Guhyakālī, O support of the jar, O you whose power is all-pervasive, O Lotus-seated One, I worship the venerable sandals! Vphreṃ Namaḥ Svāhā!*

Above that: *Rphreṃ*, obeisance to the fire-maṇḍala, the seat of the jar, which is the glorious Guhyakālī, whose self consists of ten digits (*kalā*). *Sphreṃ*, obeisance to the solar maṇḍala, the seat of the jar-nectar, which is the glorious Guhyakālī, whose self consists of twelve digits. *Phreṃ*, *phaṭ* to the setting [of the sun]. The jar.
Having washed it, place it within the mandala of the vase.
One should fill [the vessel] with purified nectar-water according to the mantra: *Phreṃ Vhrīṃ Vśrīṃ Vhnīṃ*. *Phreṃ!
Salutation to Nirvāṇa Śrī Guhyakālī, the nectar of the jar, whose essence is the sixteen digits, the stainless moon.*

Having worshipped with the water from the *kalaśa*, and having worshipped in the four directions with "Phreṃ Vhrīṃ," one should write "Kphreṃ" within the triangle in the water of the *kalaśa*. Visualizing it as nectar, one worships Amṛtakālī.

She possesses two hands displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness while holding the nectar; she is dark-complexioned, three-eyed, adorned with various ornaments, and seated upon a red lotus.
Having meditated thus, one should worship with the five offerings using this mantra: *oṃ vākyaṃ phreṃ amṛtakāli yogeśvari vphreṃ namaḥ svāhā*. Then, touching the mouth of the *kalaśa* [vase]:

Having invoked [the deity] with the *bhījonīmudrā* or the *matsyamudrā*, [one should know]: Viṣṇu resides at the mouth of the jar, Rudra is situated at the neck, Brahmā is stationed at the base, and the host of Mothers occupies the middle.
The entire ocean is its belly, and the earth with its seven continents is its body.
The Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, and likewise the Atharvaveda— all these, together with Agni, have taken refuge within this entire water-pot.
O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Godāvarī, Sarasvatī, Narmadā, Sindhu, Kāverī, and Jāhnavī, please be present here.
At the end, [he should show] fivefold: the mudrās of the boon, fearlessness, the nectar-pot, the cow, the liṅga, and the yoni.
The ritual procedure for the installation of the water-pot is completed.

Now, the ritual for establishing the conch (*śaṅkhasthāpana*): Having drawn a circle, a triangle, a ten-petaled lotus, and a square, one should worship the mandala with the mantra: "Phreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ! I worship and propitiate the sandals of the venerable Guhyakālī, the general support of the conch, whose seat is the lotus of all powers; Phreṃ Namaḥ Svāhā! Thus, having worshipped the mandala.
*Phraṃḥ astrāya phaṭ.* *Pheṃ thrīṃ*, I establish the sandals (*pādukā*) of Śrī Guhyakālī upon the tripod (*tripādikā*); *namaḥ*.

Having placed the tripod within the mandala, [one should offer] above it: *Rphreṃ*, *namaḥ* to the fire-mandala (*vahnimaṇḍala*), the general conch-throne (*sāmānya-śaṅkhāsana*) for Śrī Guhyakālī, whose nature consists of the ten digits (*daśakalātman*). One should join [the mantras].

Taking up the conch shell: *Śphreṃ khhrīṃ khaṃ khaṃ khaṃ cara cara bhrama bhrama mama śatru trāsaya trāsaya śphreṃ namaḥ svāhā*. Having thus whirled it three times in the air: *Śphreṃ śhrīṃ khphrīṃ śrīṃ guhyakāli, I establish the general arghya conch; namaḥ*.

Having placed [the vessel] upon a tripod with this mantra: *Śphreṁ Phreṁ! Obeisance to the sun-maṇḍala, the seat of nectar consisting of the general conch-offering for the glorious Guhyakālī, whose essence is the twelve digits.*

Having worshipped in the center of the conch: *Śphreṃ śaṅkhini kāli vidmahe brahmanādini dhīmahi tannaḥ śaṅkhaḥ pracodayāt*. Then, filling the conch with water: *Hrīṃ khhrīṃ vhrīṃ*. [I offer] this general conch-offering (*śaṅkhārgha*) of nectar to Śrī Guhyakālī, whose essence consists of sixteen digits (*kalā*).
Homage to the Moon Mandala. [It is] to be worshipped. Śrīṃ Khhrīṃ Vhrīṃ, homage to the worship of the conch.
Having written "vphreṃ" within a triangle in the water of a conch, one should meditate as follows: "O Kālī, whose mouth is the nectar-conch!

You who are presented with the *dhenu-mudrā*, the *karttī*, and the skull-cup; you who sit upon a white lotus throne, possess three eyes, and are adorned with all ornaments. Having thus meditated and invoked her, [one should perform the rite] with the *dhenu-mudrā*.
Having covered the conch water with the fire-mudrā, one should recite the mantra.
Brāhmī resides at the base of the conch, Lakṣmī rests upon the water within the conch, and Raudrī is situated at the tip of the conch; thus these three goddesses are fully established there.

*Gaṅge ca*, etc. *Śphreṃ khhrīṃ vhrīṃ vlīṃ kgrīṃ śaṅkhamukhi kāli parabrahmani nādini śaṅkhajalāmṛtaṃ kuru (2) śphreṃ namaḥ svāhā.* Having displayed the *karttī*, *kapāla*, *dhenu*, *śaṅkha*, *liṅga*, and *yonimudrās*, [one recites]: *vphreṃ amṛtalakṣmi vidhame*.

"O you who flow with nectar, we meditate upon you; may that Sudhā inspire us. With this mantra, having poured one-third of the water from the conch into the pitcher, [he should perform the ritual] with the remaining water: "Vphreṃ, we know the Yoginī of Nectar, the secret Kali of Nectar..."

We meditate upon that; may Siddhi inspire us. Having sprinkled the materials for worship and the deity’s chamber with water, one should cleanse the conch with the Astra-mantra and place it upon a tripod. "Vphreṃ! We know Siddhilakṣmī; we meditate upon Sudhāguhyakālī; may that Siddhi inspire us. Thus.

Having filled [the vessel] with conch-water and having written *vphreṃ* within a triangle, worship it five times with the mantras *śphreṃ*, *khhrīṃ*, and *vhrīṃ*. Then, having worshipped with the mantra: *vphreṃ amṛtaguhyakāli śrīpādukāṃ jayāmi vphreṃ namaḥ svāhā*, display the *dhenu*, *liṅga*, *śaṅkha*, and *yoni* mudrās. *Dhrīṃ*.

One should cast *dūrvā* grass into the water for the bathing of the Goddess Kucce. The procedure for the installation of the conch (*śaṅkha*) is complete. Now, the installation of the *argha* offering is written: *Phraṃḥ astāya phaṭ*. Having drawn a triangle within a circle on the ground, [one recites]: *Rphreṃ daśalānmane śammulāya*.

I worship the Śrīpādukā; *namaḥ*. *Phaiḥ*! To the weapon, *phaṭ*! O Earth, I establish the three-legged stand. *Spheṃ*, [I offer] clarified butter. *Phreṃ*! *Dhūṃ* (twice)! To the enclosure of smoke, *svāhā*! *Aphreṃ*! I establish the special vessel for the *arghya* offering. *Rphreṃ*! To the one whose self consists of the ten kalās.
*Oṃ* obeisance to the fire-maṇḍala. *Vphreṃ*, we know Yogeśvarī; we meditate upon Śrī Guhyakālī;

may she impel our success. One should write *vphreṃ* within a triangle in the midst of the water. *Vphreṃ vhkṣmlvryūṃ vhrīṃ vśrīṃ vklīṃ*, O Amṛtaguhyakālī, O Amṛta Śrīguhyabhairavārya, *strāgakṣa*, obeisance!

Svāhā! One should display the *āvāhana* (invocation) mudrā. Vphreṃ! To Amṛtaguhyakālī, [I offer] the seat (*āsana*), water for the feet (*pādya*), and so forth—perfume (*gandha*), flowers (*puṣpa*), incense (*dhūpa*), lamps (*dīpa*), food offerings (*naivedya*), and betel leaf (*tāmbūla*)—obeisance! [Recite] *Gaṅge ca* and so forth. Oṃ! We know Kālarātri; we meditate upon Kālasaṃkarṣaṇī; may that Kālī inspire us.

The threefold consecration (*abhimantraṇa*). One should display the cow, the linga, the yoni, and the fish mudrās. The installation of the *argha* vessel is complete. *Phreṃ Ghhrīṃ*, I worship the venerable sandals of the goddess Ghaṇṭādevī.
Having offered a handful of flowers at the auspicious door, one should proceed as follows.

Having stabilized the water in a cloth-strained water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*) by means of drying and other methods, one should write the syllable *vphreṃ* in that water. After consecrating that water three times with mantras and displaying the *dhenu*, *liṅga*, and *yoginī* mudrās, one should [draw] on the ground in front of the Goddess, or to her left side, using vermilion, red sandalwood paste, *tūrī*, or honey mixed with water.
Or: Having marked a circle with a drop, eight petals, and a square, [and having invoked] *pheṃ hrīṃ śrī hlīṃ*,
I worship the lotus-seated *śrīpādukā* of the special *arghya*-supporting power (*viśeṣārghyādhāraśakti*) of Śrī Guhyakālī.

Having worshipped the maṇḍala: *Phreṃḥ Astāya Phaṭ*. With this, one washes the tripod (*tripādikā*) and the vessel for the offering water (*arghyapātra*). *Phreṃ Thrīṃ*, I establish the tripod. Having placed it upon the maṇḍala with fish, power-substances (*śakti*), flowers, and so forth: *Sphreṃ Kphreṃ Khphreṃ Vphreṃ Hreṃ*, I purify the vessel for the offering water with the essence. *Rphreṃ*.
Sprinkling with the net [mudrā] and so forth: *Phreṃ Dhūṃ* (twice), *Dhumāvatī svāhā*. Offering the water for honor (*arghya*) and burning incense: *Phreṃ Khhrīṃ* (thrice), *Bhāmyākoṇe*. Three times:
(1) *Śrīguhyakāliviśeṣārghyaṃ sthāpayāmi śrīguhyakāli prasīda* (twenty-one times), *namaḥ svāhā*.

Thus, one should place the tripod. *Rphreṃ*, obeisance to the seat of the vessel for the offering (*arghya*) for the fire-mandala consisting of ten digits (*kalā*). *Sphreṃ*, obeisance to the seat of the nectar of the offering for the sun-mandala consisting of twelve digits. One should worship [these] in the middle of the vessel.
With the purified nectars and so forth: (1) *Vphreṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ Vhkṣmlvryūṃ Amṛtayogeśvari* (2) *Amṛtavarṣa* (2) *Vphreṃ Namaḥ Svāhā*. One should fill the vessel.
*Sphraiṃ*, obeisance to the lunar maṇḍala consisting of sixteen digits, the special *arghya* nectar for Śrī Guhyakālī;
[thus] worship. Within the nectar of the vessel, one should visualize a triangle surrounded by a pentagon and a square.

Having written *vphraiṃ* within a triangle and [the mantras] *hsṣmlvryūṃ* and *vhkṣmlvryūṃ*, one should point toward it. Therein, in the nectar (*amṛta*), having placed *phreṃ śrīṃ māṃ* or *saṃkhaṃ* or *vā* or *ṭ-hrīṃ*, or a piece of ginger, cardamom, and so forth, therein is Amṛteśvarī.

One should worship. VPHREṂ VIJAṂ | VHRĪṂ. For this mantra of Amṛteśvarī, Dhanañjaya is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ), and Amṛteśvarī is the deity (devatā). VPHREṂ VIJAṂ | VHRĪṂ is the power (śakti). VHKLVRŪṂ is the peg (kīlakaṃ). This is the special arghya for Śrī Guhyakālī.

The application (*viniyoga*) is for the worship of Amṛteśvarī for the sake of attaining success through the deceased (*mṛtasiddhi*). *Vhrāṃ*—the ritual assignment (*nyāsa*) of the hands. *Vhrīṃ*—the ritual assignment of the heart and other limbs (*hṛdayādinyāsa*).
Meditative absorption.
Indeed, for those seated upon red lotuses, the radiance is like that of a flickering flame.
Likewise, there are two jars of nectar and two red lotuses.
Holding [a lotus] with her glorious fingertips, her lotus-face adorned with a gentle smile,
she is endowed with a crown of rubies and has the crescent moon as her crest-ornament.

I worship with supreme faith and devotion Amṛteśvarī, who is enriched by the splendor of anklets, clad in yellow garments, adorned with ornaments of various jewels, and the bestower of all spiritual attainments.
Thus ends the section on meditative concentration.

*vphreṁ vhrīṁ vhkṣmlvryūṁ śrī klīṁ amṛtakarāli amṛtayogeśvari hūṁ saḥ phreṁ namaḥ svāhā*. Having worshipped her with this mantra of Amṛteśvarī, one should invoke the nectar residing in the vessel with this same mantra and worship it with the fivefold offerings (*pañcopacāra*).

Having consecrated the nectar (sudhā) contained in the vessel five times by touching it with the Yonimudrā while reciting the mantra, one should then display the Padmamudrā, Kalśamudrā, Dhenumudrā, Liṅgamudrā, and Yonimudrā.
By means of this [mantra], one should offer the specific [oblation] situated in the vessel: (1) *Vphreṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ*, I satisfy the glorious Guhyakālī; homage!
One should satisfy [the deity] in three ways. With "Pūjā Sāmeśrī Vphreṃ," one sprinkles [it]. Again, with "Vphreṃ Kavacāya Hūṃ," one covers the distinguished nectar with the armor-mantra.

VPHREIḤ ASTĀYA PHAṬ. Protect with the weapon-mantra (astra). One should perform the worship of the Root Goddess preceded by the consecration and offering of the *bali*. YHRĪṂ VHRĪṂ: having purified the impurity residing in the food through drying and burning; then VHRĪṂ: having performed the immersion with water, unbroken rice, and flowers; PHREṂḤ: for the weapon-mantra.

*Phaṭ!* [This is for] the vessels for the *bali* offerings washed with the weapon-mantra (*astra*), those situated before the Goddesses, those in the southeast, southwest, and those gone to the cremation ground, as well as the vessels of Gaṇeśa, Vaṭuka, the Kṣetrapālas, and the Yoginīs; and in the vessel situated in the midst of these, [are] the Root Goddess and Bhairava.

Having prepared the cooked rice in two vessels and filled them up to the Bhairava-vessel with *vhrīṃ* for Gaṇeśa, together with black-gram balls (*māṣavaṭaka*) and other offerings, one should pour [the essence] into the root-vessel with the root mantra: *vhrīṃ vhrīṃ vśrīṃ vklīṃ puryāt*.

In the center of the root-offering (*mūlabali*), one should draw a triangle and write the *mūlakuṭa* (the seed-syllable) surrounded by *vhkṣmlvryūṃ*. Outside the triangle, one should draw a circle; within its four petals, one should write *vhrīṃ*, *vśrīṃ*, and *klīṃ*, and on the outer petals, one should write *hūṃ*, *saḥ*, and *phreṃ*. Outside of that is a circle.

In the center of the square *bhairava* offering vessel, one should write the syllable *vhrīṃ* within a circle in the middle; then, surround it from the outside with the *bhairava-kūṭa*. Furthermore, in the centers of the vessels for Gaṇeśa and the others, one should write *vhrīṃ vhrīṃ*.
Having visualized those foods contained in the offering vessels as consisting of nectar: *Vphreṃ VhKṣmLvryūṃ Vhrī Vhrīṃ Vklīṃ HSkṣmLvryūṃ! Come, come, O Amṛtayogeśvarī!
Behold these foods and so forth situated in the offering vessels; (2) transform them into nectar.* (2)

"Amṛtabhairavāya amṛtabhairavyai juṃ saḥ vphreṃ namaḥ svāhā. Having thus touched the food and other offerings contained in the *bali* vessel while reciting [the mantra], one should then perform the *dhenu*, *liṅga*, and *yoni* mudrās three times. "Vphreṃ: hūṃ, protect from within with the armor! "Vphreṃ: aḥ, protect thoroughly with the weapon!"

With *yhrīṃ rhrīṃ vhrīṃ*, one should perform the drying and burning of the substance and impurity through the Vidyā. [Then, with] scented water, flowers, and water: *vphreṃ yogeśvarī vidmahe śrīguhyakālī dhīmahi tanno siddhiḥ pracodayāt*.

In the offerings such as the bell and others, one should draw a triangle and write "vphreṃ" in its center; having consecrated it with this [mantra], one should display the Dhenu, Liṅga, and Yoginī mudrās. "Phreṃ Ghhrīṃ, I worship the venerable sandals of the goddess Ghaṭādevī; [to] the bell. The bell.

Having worshipped, display the *dhenu-mudrā* and ring the bell. *vphreṃ vhrīṃ vśrīṃ vklīṃ* Śrī Guhyakālī, Śrīmadvajrakapāṭeśvarī, bearer of the trident, skull-cup, sword, and shield, three-eyed one, blaze! (2) Arise, arise, Śrī Guhyakālī, for the sake of worship, Śrī Guhyakālī!
Open the glorious Vajrakapāṭa door! Expel Brahmā and the others, as well as the Piśācas and the rest!

This door, worshipped by various [beings], possessing a mandala of light from diverse jewels, flashing like lightning, fashioned by Viśvakarman, and resplendent with the glory of Śrī Lakṣmī—open this glorious jewel-door! (2)
Vajrayoginī vphreṃ namaḥ svāhā. With this mantra, one should worship with flowers at the door.
Having displayed the Liṅgayoni-mudrā and performed the three *tāla* strikes preceded by the sound of the bell.
Having opened the glorious door and prostrated with the five mudrās before the root goddesses: *Hphreṃ!
Homage to Sāmalasya-nirvāṇa-śrī-guhyakālī and Bhairava-śrī-guhyakālī!* [With palms joined in añjali.]
Furthermore, one should please the goddesses, beginning with Nalādevī, by means of their respective mudrās.
Kāli, Mahākāli, Guhyakāli, Kumālike!
O Siddhiguhyamahākālī, O Siddhilakṣmī, O Kuleśvarī!
Grant devotion to the pair of your lotus feet; be gracious to me.
Having praised the Goddess with joined palms: *Hphreṁ*, I worship and satisfy the *śrīpādukā* of the glorious Guhyakālī, the glory of Nirvāṇa;
*Hphreṁ Namaḥ Svāhā*. [Offering] flowers, one should present them. [Then, one should display] the cow-seal (*dhenumudrā*), the liṅga-seal (*liṅgamudrā*), and the womb-seal (*yonimudrā*).

She who grants the fruit of the four aims to those who worship her lotus feet;
the maiden Śrī Guhyakālī, greatly beloved by the great Bhoga;

(1) *Vphreṃ* *vhkṣmlvryūṃ*, may the Lord of the Reality of Self (*ātmatattva*), Nirvāṇaśrī Guhyakālī, be satisfied! (1) *Vphreṃ* *vhkṣmlvryūṃ*, may the Lord of the Reality of Knowledge (*vidyātattva*), Nirvāṇaśrī Guhyakālī, be satisfied!
(1) vphreṃ vhkṣmlvryūṃ, may the Lord of the Śiva-tattva, Nirvāṇaśrī Guhyakālī, be satisfied!
(1) vphreṃ vhkṣmlvryūṃ malavarayūṃ || May the Lord of all principles, Nirvāṇaśrī Guhyakālī,
be satisfied!
(1) Vphreṃ Vhkṣmlvryūṃ! O Nirvāṇaśrī Guhyakālī, may the maṇḍala of the lion-faced ones be satisfied!
(1) vphreṁ vhkṣmlvryūṁ; may the maṇḍala of Heruka with faces [like those of] lions, the secret Kālī Nirvāṇaśrī, be satisfied.
(1) vphreṁ vhkṣmlvryūṁ; may the Nirvāṇaśrī Guhyakālī and the assembly of divine faces be satisfied.
(1) vphreṁ vhkṣmlvryūṁ; may Nirvāṇaśrī Guhyakālī and the mandala of the locust-faced ones be satisfied.
(1) vphreṁ vhkṣmlvryūṁ; may the maṇḍala of the tiger-faced Nirvāṇaśrī Guhyakālī be satisfied!
(1) vphreṃ vhkṣmlvryūṃ, O Nirvāṇaśrī Guhyakālī, may the maṇḍala of the makara-face be satisfied!
(1) vphreṃ vhkṣmlvryūṃ, may the Nirvāṇaśrī Guhyakālī and the circle of bear-faced deities be satisfied!
(1) vphreṁ vhkṣmlvryūṁ; may the maṇḍala of Nirvāṇaśrī Guhyakālī with the monkey face be satisfied.
(1) vphreṁ vhkṣmlvryūṁ; may Nirvāṇaśrīguhyakālī and the Tārkṣyamukha maṇḍala be satisfied.
(1) VPHREṂ VHKṢMLVRYŪṂ! O Nirvāṇaśrī Guhyakālī, may the mandala of the sow-faced goddess be satisfied!
(1) vphreṁ vhkṣmlvryūṁ: May the Hayamukha maṇḍala of Nirvāṇaśrīguhyakālī be satisfied!
(1) vphreṁ vhkṣmlvryūṁ: O Nirvāṇaśrī Guhyakālī, may the mandala of Gajamukha be satisfied!
(1) vphreṁ vhkṣmlvryūṁ; O Nirvāṇaśrī Guhyakālī, may the human-faced maṇḍala be satisfied!

(1) vphreṃ vhkṣmlvryūṃ, O Nirvāṇaśrī Guhyakālī Bhairava, may you be satisfied!

May they be satisfied! (1) VPHREṂ VHKṢMLVRYŪṂ Ātmanirvāṇaśrīguhyakālī, may you be satisfied!

Thus, one should place [the offering] upon one’s own head. Preceded by meditation on the *ṛṣi*, *chandas*, and other attributes of the root mantra, one should recite the root mantra as many times as possible. Having offered the flowers held in the hands to the Goddess, one should contemplate the *naivedya* (food offering) as having been enjoyed at will by the Supreme Sovereign. *Vphreṁ namaḥ svadhā*.

VPHREṂ. One should offer water for the hand of the Goddess. Having dismissed the food offering (naivedya), one should offer water with VPHREṂ for the purpose of washing the hands and rinsing the mouth of the Goddess’s consort, Śrī Makhayā. Having performed the purification of the place where the food offering was kept, one should offer water for the hand of the Goddess with the mantra: VPHREṂ NAMAḤ SVADHĀ.

Threefold: (1) O Śrī Guhyakālī, I offer this betel leaf (*tāmbūla*) to you; *namaḥ svāhā*. [This is] the betel leaf. O Śrī Guhyakālī, giver of boons, you who delight in supreme nectar, my beloved Mother, grant me permission for the worship of my retinue.
Having obtained permission, one should perform the worship of the selection (*varaṇa-pūjā*).
(1) vphreṃ hasakṣamalavarayūṃ | kphreṃ, O Sovereign of all mantras, tantras, and yantras, Nirvāṇaśrī Guhyakālī, I worship and propitiate the Śrīpādukā; (1) namaḥ svāhā.

Having worshipped the Root Goddess once, and having bowed with the Liṅga-yoni mudrā, [one offers] *phreṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ* to the sandals of the Yoginīs of the entire tradition of the manifest, hidden, and secret, of the Kula, Kaula, Nirgarbha, Rahasya, and Atirahasya: *namaḥ*. Having worshipped once, one bows with the Dhenu-liṅga-yoni mudrā.
The goddess's enclosure is a triangle; outside of that, in the eight petals, there are four [petals] in the corners starting from the southeast and four in the intermediate directions.
Hphrā hṛdayāya namaḥ | Hphrīṃ sirase svāhā | Hphrūṃ śikhāyai ṣaṭ | Hphreṃ kavacāya hūṃ | Hphrauṃ netratrayāya vaṣaṭ | Hphreṃḥ astrāya phaṭ | Having thus worshipped:
In the triangle, in the three corners: (1) O Śrī Guhyakālī of the Self-Nirvāṇa, I worship and satisfy the Śrī Pādukā; namaḥ svāhāḥ. (1) Ananta.
(1) Vphreṁ, O Śrī Guhyakālī of the Supreme Self-Nirvāṇa, I worship and satisfy the Śrī Pādukā; namaḥ.
Svāhā! (1) O Śrī Guhyakālī, whose self is immediate nirvāṇa, I worship and satiate the venerable sandals. (1) Namaḥ svāhā! [At] the five-petaled [lotus].
*Sphreṃ*, I worship and propitiate the venerable *Sṛṣṭikālī-śrīpādukā*; *sphreṃ* (1) *namaḥ svāhā*. *Sphreṃ*, I worship and propitiate the venerable *Sthitikālī-śrīpādukā*; *sphreṃ* *namaḥ*.
Svāhā! Sphreṃ! I worship and satisfy the venerable sandals of Saṃhārakālī; Sphreṃ! (1) Namaḥ Svāhā! Sphreṃ! I worship and satisfy the venerable sandals of Anākṣyākālī;
Sphreṃ! (1) Namaḥ Svāhā! Rphreṃ! I worship the venerable sandals of Bhāsākālī.
I satisfy: rphreṃ (1) namaḥ svāhā. [In the six corners.]
Yphreṃ, I worship and satiate the sandals of the venerable Yogeśvarī; yphreṃ, obeisance, svāhā!
Sphreṃ, I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of the Great Mistress of Yoga; Sphreṃ, obeisance, svāhā!
Cphreṃ! I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of Caṇḍayogeśvarī; rphreṃ! obeisance, svāhā! Sphreṃ! I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī; sphreṃ! obeisance, svāhā!
*Kphreṃ*, I worship and propitiate the *śrīpādukā* of Kālacaṇḍayogeśvarī Śrī Guhyakālī;
*kphreṃ namaḥ svāhā*. *Sphreṃ*, I worship and propitiate the *śrīpādukā* of Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī;
*sphreṃ namaḥ svāhā*. *Yphreṃ*, I worship the *śrīpādukā* of Yoginī.

I satiate yphreṃ; obeisance, svāhā! Sphreṃ, I worship and satiate the śrīpādukā of Mahāyoginī; sphreṃ, obeisance, svāhā! Cphreṃ, I worship and satiate the śrīpādukā of Caṇḍayoginī; cphreṃ, obeisance, svāhā! Sphreṃ, [I worship and satiate] Mahācaṇḍayoginī...
I worship and satiate the venerable sandals; *sphreṃ* homage! *svāhā*. *kphreṃ*, I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of Kālacaṇḍayoginī; *kphreṃ* homage! *svāhā*.
Sphreṃ! I worship and satiate the *śrīpādukā* of Mahākāla Caṇḍayoginī; Sphreṃ! Namaḥ Svāhā. [In the hexagon.]
Pphreṃ, I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of Pūrṇeśvarī; pphreṃ, obeisance, svāhā! Nphreṃ, I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of Niśeśvarī; nphreṃ, obeisance, svāhā!
KPHREṂ, I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of Kubjeśvarī; KPHREṂ, obeisance, svāhā!
Sphreṃ! O Siddhilakṣmī, I worship and satiate the venerable pādukā; Sphreṃ! Namaḥ svāhā!
KPHREṂ, I worship and propitiate the venerable sandals of Kāmeśvarī; KPHREṂ, salutation, svāhā!
vphreṃ, I worship and satisfy the venerable sandals of Vajrayoginī; kphreṃ, homage! svāhā!
On the eight-petaled [lotus]: KPHREṂ, I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of Kālī; KPHREṂ, obeisance, svāhā!
Sphreṃ, I worship and satisfy the auspicious sandals of Mahākālī; Sphreṃ, obeisance, svāhā!
Cphreṃ Caṇḍakālī, I worship and satiate the venerable pādukā; rphreṃ, obeisance, svāhā!
Sphreṃ, I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of Mahācaṇḍakālī; Sphreṃ, namaḥ svāhā!
Vphreṃ, I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of Kālacaṇḍakālī; Kphreṃ, namaḥ svāhā!

Sphrai! I worship and satisfy the venerable sandals of Mahākāla Caṇḍakālī; Sphrai! Namaḥ Svāhā! Rphreṃ! I worship and satisfy the venerable sandals of Bhadrakālī; Rphreṃ! Namaḥ Svāhā! Sphreṃ! I worship the venerable sandals of Siddhikālī.

I satiate: *sphreṃ* namaḥ svāhā. On the eight-petaled [lotus], *aphraṃ*: I worship and satiate the venerable sandal of Brahmavatī for Asitāṅga Bhairava; *aphraṃ* namaḥ svāhā. *Rphreṃ*: I worship and satiate the venerable sandal of Rudravatī for Ruru Bhairava.

I worship and satiate the venerable sandals; *rphreṃ* *namaḥ* *svāhā*. *Sphreṃ*, to Saṃhārabhairava, O Lakṣmīvati, I worship and satiate the venerable sandals; *sphreṃ* *namaḥ* *svāhā*.

Upon the tips of the tridents: PHREṂ VHRĪṂ, I worship and satisfy the venerable sandals of the Vajra; VHRĪṂ NAMAḤ SVĀHĀ. Svāhā! Phreṃ Khhrīṃ, I worship and satisfy the venerable sandals of the sword; Khhrīṃ, obeisance, svāhā!

Namaḥ svāhā. Phreṃ at the eight directions of the door. Phreṃ k(-)hrīṃ: I worship and satiate the venerable sandal of the Karavīra cremation ground; k(-)hreṃ namaḥ svāhā. Phreṃ jphrīṃ: I worship and satiate the venerable sandal of the Jayāvaha cremation ground; j(-)hrīṃ namaḥ svāhā.

Phreṃ K-hrīṃ, I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of the Kāladaṇḍa cremation ground; K-hrīṃ, homage! Svāhā! Phreṃ K-hrīṃ, I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of the Kālapāśa cremation ground; K-hrīṃ, homage! Svāhā! Phreṃ N-hrīṃ, [I worship] Lakṣmī’s Vaśmaśāna...

I worship and satiate the Śrīpādukā; *nhrīṃ* namaḥ svāhā. *Phreṃ dhhrīṃ*, I worship and satiate the Śrīpādukā of the Dhūmra-ākula cremation ground; *dhhrīṃ* namaḥ svāhā. *Phreṃ ahrīṃ*, I worship and satiate the Śrīpādukā of the Asipatra (Sword-leaf) cremation ground.
Ahrīṃ namaḥ svāhā. Phreṃ vhrīṃ, I worship and satiate the śrīpādukā of the Bhūtāvaha cremation ground; vhrīṃ namaḥ svāhā. Phreṃ k(-)hrīṃ, obeisance to the Muṇḍa of the Kṛtayuga.

Phreṃ t-thrīṃ, obeisance to the shaven-headed one of the Tretā Yuga. Phreṃ d-hrīṃ, obeisance to the shaven-headed one of the Dvāpara Yuga. Phreṃ k-hrīṃ, obeisance to the shaven-headed one of the Kali Yuga. Phreṃ ṛ-hrīṃ, obeisance to the shaven-headed one of the Ṛgveda.
Phreṃ jhrīṃ, obeisance to the Muṇḍa of the Yajurveda! Phreṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to the Muṇḍa of the Sāmaveda!
Phreṃ Ahrīṃ Arthavveda, obeisance to Muṇḍā! Phreṃ Iṃ, obeisance to Indramuṇḍāsana!
Phreṃ Ahrīṃ, obeisance to Agnimuṇḍa! Phreṃ Ṭhrīṃ, obeisance to Yamamuṇḍa!
Phreṃ Nhrīṃ, salutation to Muṇḍā of the Nairṛti [direction]. Phreṃ Vhrīṃ, salutation to Muṇḍā of Varuṇa. Phreṃ Vhrīṃ, salutation to Muṇḍā of Vāyu. Phreṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to Muṇḍā of Soma.
Phreṃ I Hrīṃ, obeisance to Īśāna-muṇḍa! Phreṃ Vhrīṃ, obeisance to Brahma-muṇḍa! Phreṃ Vhrīṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu-muṇḍa!
Phreṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Sṛṣṭimuṇḍa! Phreṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Sthitīmuṇḍa! Phreṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Saṃhāramuṇḍa! Phreṃ Ahrīṃ, obeisance to Anākhyāmuṇḍa!
Phreṃ Rhrīṃ, obeisance to Bhāsāmuṇḍa! Phreṃ Vhrīṃ, obeisance to Brahmapretāsana! Phreṃ Vhrīṃ...

Salutation to the corpse-seat of Viṣṇu. Phreṃ rhrīṃ, salutation to the corpse-seat of Rudra. Phreṃ śrīṃ, salutation to the corpse-seat of Sadāśiva. Phreṃ rhrīṃ, salutation to the corpse-seat of Bhairava. Phreṃ śhrīṃ, salutation to the corpse-seat of Śivā. Phreṃ hrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ, [salutation to] Śrī Guhyakālī.
I worship and satiate the sandals of Śrīpādukā, the youthful Fortune of Dharma; *phreṃ* *namaḥ* *svāhā*.

Phreṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Śrīṃ, I worship and satiate the sandals of the venerable Guhyakālī Kāmalakṣmīdvāla; Phreṃ Namaḥ Svāhā! Phreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ, I worship and satiate the sandals of the venerable Guhyakālī Mokṣalakṣmīdvāla; Phreṃ Namaḥ Svāhā!

Phreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ, I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of Śrī Guhyakālī, the gateway to the Lakṣmī of Sālokya; Phreṃ Namaḥ Svāhā. Phreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of the gateway to the Lakṣmī of Sāyujya.
I worship, I satisfy: *phreṃ namaḥ svāhā*. *Phreṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ*, I worship, I satisfy the sandals (*śrīpādukā*) of Sāmipya-lakṣmī-dvāra: *phreṃ namaḥ svāhā*.
Phreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ, I worship and satisfy the sandals of the auspicious Śrī at the gateway of the Lakṣmī of Similarity; Phreṃ Namaḥ Svāhā.
The entire ocean, the earth with its seven continents, the Ṛgveda, Yajurveda, Sāmaveda,
and Atharvaveda— all these, together with the Aṅgas, took refuge within the water-pot.

Having recited "Gaṅge ca" and so forth, and having consecrated [the water] with the Gāyatrī mantra: "Vphreṃ, we know Caṇḍakapālinī; we meditate upon Guhyakālī; may she, the Nectar (Sudhā), inspire us," one should sprinkle the water in the jar three times while forming the Kubha, Dhenu, Liṅga, and Yoni mudrās over the jar.
In his own portion, he should place the conch and the general vessel.
[Thus ends the eleventh chapter, the procedure for the installation of the general jar, in the section on initiation within the glorious Uttaranirvāṇasaṃhitā.]

O Bhairavī, listen to the procedure for the placement of the vessel common to the conch by Bhairava: having fashioned a circular mandala of the earth-element on the ground to your right side, marked with the syllable *hrīṃ* and adorned with three lines, using the fish-seal (*matsyamudrā*);
then, supporting it with the thumb of the right hand, take scents, leaves, and other offerings with the left hand.

*Phreṃ*. O Śrī Guhyakālī, I worship the *śrīpādukā* resting upon the lotus of all powers (*sarvaśakti*) on the mandala of the base of the common vessel (*sāmānyapātra*) within the conch; *namaḥ*. Having thus offered flowers, take up the conch that has been washed eight times over it. *Phreṃ*. O Śrī Guhyakālī, [the conch...]

"I place the three-legged stand, the support for the general vessel; homage! Having thus placed the three-legged stand, [one should apply] the powder upon its mandala. Upon that: *Phreṃ Rhrīṃ*, to the ten-syllabled self, the Śrī Guhyakālī conch, the seat of the general vessel.
"Salutation to the fire-maṇḍala. Having thus worshipped it, one should take up the conch shell purified by the weapon-mantra (astra).
*Phreṃ śphreṃ*, obeisance to Mahāśaṅkhamukhī Kālī. Having thus whirled [the mantra] three times in the sky.

*Phreṃ rśa śrīguhyakāli śaṅkhasāmānyapātraṃ sthāpayāmi namaḥ.* Having thus placed it upon the tripod (*tripādikā*): *Phreṃ ha śrīdvādaśakalātmane śrīguhyakāli-śaṅkha-sāmānyapātrāmṛtāsanāya sūryamaṇḍalāya namaḥ.* Having thus worshipped within the vessel:
"Phreṃ Śphreṃ, obeisance to Mahāśaṅkhamukhī Kālī. Thus, one should worship her with conch-shell powder, scents, unbroken rice, and other offerings.

With water purified by the *gāyatrī* mantra, one should worship [the vessel] with: "Phreṃ! O Śrī Guhyakālī, I worship the general vessel (sāmānyapātra) in the conch; obeisance! Having thus worshipped, one should worship the water situated within the conch with: "Phreṃ Vhrīṃ! O Śrī Guhyakālī, obeisance to the deceased (mṛtāya) in the general vessel within the conch. Therein—
One should write "vphreṃ" within a triangle. Brāhmī, together with Brahmā, is established at the base of the conch;
Mahālakṣmī, together with Viṣṇu, is established in the middle of the conch.

The tip of the conch is eternally established as if by Śaṅkara himself; therefore, one should contemplate that water as being nectar. Phreṃ, salutation to Gaṅgā. Phreṃ, salutation to Yamunā. Phreṃ, salutation to Godāvarī. Phreṃ, salutation to Sarasvatī. Phreṃ, salutation to Narmadā.

Homage! *Phreṃ*, homage to Sindhu; *phreṃ*, homage to Kāverī; thus one should worship the Seven Gaṅgās there. Having consecrated [the water] seven times with "vphreṃ," one should cover it with the fish-mudrā (*matsyamudrā*).
Salutations to [the deity] beginning with the act of gazing.

Thus, having performed the worship, one should display the conch, cow, liṅga, and yoni mudrās; then, having poured the remaining water back into the vessel, one should sprinkle the ritual materials used for the consecrated worship with the mantra *phaṭ phreṃ miṭ*. Then, [one should likewise sprinkle] oneself.
Having washed the conch and placed it upon a tripod, [one should worship] with the water from the *kalaśa* vessel: (1) *Hskṣmlvryūṃ Vphreṃ Vhksmlvryūṃ Śrī*.
Thus, having worshipped the conch, [one should worship] within its center, in a triangle: (1) *Hma* (six times). Thus, one should encircle it.
In those three corners, one should write VPHREṂ, VPHRĪṂ, and VHRĪṂ. In the east, one should worship with perfumes and other offerings that which is invoked.

Having consecrated [the substances] with the five seed-syllables: *ḥ* (1), *hma* (6), *vphreṃ*, *vhrīṃ* (6), *śrī*; [one says]: *Phreṃ*, obeisance to the incense (*dhūpa*). To the nectar in the conch (*śaṅkhāmṛta*): *Phreṃ da-hrīṃ*, obeisance to the lamp (*dīpa*) for the nectar in the conch.
Having thus offered the lamp with the syllable *oṃ*, and having displayed the *dhenu*, *śaṅkha*, *liṅga*, and *yonimudrās*,
one should establish the vessel for the special *arghya*. Thus ends the twelfth chapter, the procedure for establishing the ordinary conch-vessel, in the venerable *Uttaranirvāṇasaṃhitā*.
[The chapter is completed.]
Bhairavī: Salutations to you, the supreme liberator from the bonds of the individual soul (paśu) toward ultimate auspiciousness;
for those scorched by the sun of the three afflictions, you alone are the supreme refuge.
Having spoken thus, I pay homage to the pair [of feet] that rescue one from the ocean of saṃsāra.
Salutations to you, the mother who uplifts [the world] and bestows the fruits of the four aims of human life.
Place the vessel of the specific offering; tell me with honey.
O Bhairava, by the mere act of establishing it, Guhyakālī becomes well-pleased.
This is to be kept strictly secret; it bestows fruits both in this world and the next.
O you who are devoted to Śrī Guhyakālī, I shall speak to you; listen further.

Through His grace, for the purpose of completing the desired rite commenced without obstacle, there is the application (*viniyoga*) for the worship of Śrī Śakti Gaṇapati. *Phreṃ gāṃ* and so forth is the finger-assignment (*aṅgulinyāsa*). With *phreṃ glāṃ* and so forth is the heart-assignment (*hṛdayādinyāsa*). [This is] the stated meditation (*dhyāna*).
Muccaran || *Phreṃ Gaṃ Glāṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ* | O Siddhi-Śmaśāna-Mahāpīṭha, seated upon the great corpse, O Śrīmac-Ciccaṇḍa-Śakti Mahā-Gaṇapati, bring all people under my control!
(2) *Namaḥ Svāhā*. Having thus invoked and worshipped [him], [one should worship] the eight-petaled [lotus] joined with the peacock-emblem in the directions.
O you who are adorned with beauty of form!
Having worshipped the six-faced one (Kumāra) in the *kalaśa* with auspicious perfumes, flowers, and other offerings:
*Phreṃ Suṃ*, to the embodiment of the vessel of nectar (*sudhākalaśamūrti*), to Subrahmaṇya, to Bhartṛkarāya: *Oṃ namo bhagavate*.

[Offer] the invocation (*āvāhana*), water for the face (*arghya*), water for the feet (*pādya*), and so forth, water for sipping (*ācamanīya*), a seat (*āsana*), the sacred thread (*upavīta*), perfume (*gandha*), flowers (*puṣpa*), incense (*dhūpa*), and a lamp (*dīpa*).
Whatever has been offered to you—the food offering, betel, circumambulation, prostrations, and so forth—may all that be complete with mantras; be gracious, be the giver of boons, and protect me.
(2) Salutations to Bhavānī, to the son of Saṃkara, to Kumāra, the Lord.
I worship the six-faced leader of the gods, who bestows all prosperity and grants victory in great battles, standing above the army of the gods.

Having thus offered praise and prostrated with the *muktā* (pearl) salutation, one should worship as follows: Within the thousand-petaled lotus (*sahasrāra-padma*), in the center of the shining jar (*kalaśa*), one should invoke and worship the Śrī Guru, beginning with Śiva. The mantra is: *Phreṃ Śrī Hrīṃ Klīṃ Śivādi-Śrī-gurubhyo namaḥ*. [Then] *Vphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ* [to the] Sudhā-kalaśa-mūrtis.
The invocation and other rites for the venerable gurus beginning with Śiva.
Meditative concentration.
I always bow to those who grant boons, holding with the tips of their hands the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, the gesture of primordial wisdom, and a skull-cup filled with honey.
And salutations to the gurus, beginning with Śiva, who are as white as alkali.
Praise.
I bow to the venerable Guru, beginning with Śiva, the sole witness of all the worlds.
They grant liberation while living and effect the release of beings from their bonds.

Having performed the worship beginning with the invocation, the knower of mantras should place [the book] upon the vessel atop the lotus pericarp, which is radiant with the hundred-syllable mantra and adorned with the book and knowledge mudrās.
There, one should invoke the five gurus, beginning with "asmacchabdādi."
*Phreṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ vphreṃ*, obeisance to the five venerable gurus, the embodiments of the nectar-flasks. Thus one should worship, preceded by meditation.
Then follows the worship of the root-vase (*mūlakalaśa*). It is as follows:

Of this Great Mantra of Śrī Guhyakālī—the embodiment of the auspicious jar of nectar and the liberation of the Supreme Brahman—Kālāgnirudra is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the unmanifest *bṛhatī* is the meter (*chandas*), and she herself is the deity (*devatā*). (1) *Vphreṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*); *Vphreṃ* is the power (*śakti*).

Hphreṃ, the Kilaka! For the attainment of the fruits of the four aims (caturvarga) for Keśa Āsya Devadatta, [I offer] the glorious Root [Mantra], the glorious Vase-form, the Supreme Brahman, Nirvāṇa, the glorious Guhyakālī, the glorious Sudhā, the glorious Jewel-vessel, and the glorious Divine Nectar-blessing; [and likewise] the glorious Root, the Sudhā-jewel, and the glorious Vase-form.
The application of the ritual procedure for the worship of Śrī Guhyakālī, the Nirvāṇa-Śrī of the Supreme Brahman.
The six-limbed *ṣaḍaṅga* finger-placement (*mudrā-nyāsa*) for the first seed-syllable (*kūṭa*). The six-limbed heart-and-other placement (*hṛdayādi-nyāsa*) for the second seed-syllable.

The third peak mantra pervades [the body] three times from the crown of the head to the feet. The mantra is as follows: (1) *kphreṃ vphreṃ mahāmṛtyuñjayāmṛta jaganmohana śrīlakṣmī parabrahma śrīguhyakāli vphreṃ amṛtasejivīniḥ namaḥ svāhā*

If one must perform the creation, maintenance, or dissolution of others through another mantra, then, having performed that,
one should again contemplate the Root Goddess in the heart with this mantra and worship her mentally.

Having caused the Goddess to descend— either through the *suṣumnā* path into the right nostril, or by means of the *supuṣpa* [flower] purified by the *karamudrā* into the midst of the flowers held in *añjali*— one should [invoke her] from the heap of flowers in the *kalaśa* with the mantra to be recited hereafter.
O Goddess, worship the glorious Mūlā, who bestows fortune, together with her retinue, within the nectar-wheel of the hand.

The mantra to be recited is as follows: (1) *Hma* 8 *Vhraṃ* *Kṣmalavarayūṃ* *Vphreṃ* *Vhrīṃ* *Vśrīṃ* *Vhlīṃ* *Vphreṃ* *Kaṃ* (2) *Kā* (2) *Gaṃ* (2) *Gāṃ* (3) *Kāli* (2) *Mahākāli* (2) *Guhyakāli* (2) *Kulādi*, arise, arise from your own seat! *Jaya* (2) *Mahāmaṅgala Guhyakāli* (2), together with your retinue!
Dance together! Descend! Come!

By way of the *suṣumṇā*, enter the handful of flowers placed upon my head through the right nostril! Look upon me with a compassionate glance! Smile beautifully! Be gracious! Enchant the three worlds!
(2) Having established [the deity] in the Śrīcakra, the king of diagrams, which is the nectar of the beautiful, radiant, and auspicious great jar, I worship:

*vphreṃ namaḥ svāhā*. Thus, having brought [the deity] down into the hand, having invoked with the previously mentioned root mantra, and then having displayed the invocation mudrā and so forth in the venerable jar, one says: *vphrāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*.
Because of its nature as a Vaiya, it belongs to the Ādityas.

Thus, having offered [the oblation] for the binding of the specific [deities], one should worship the Eye (netra) in the center of the corners beginning with the southeast, and the Entrails (antra) in front: *Vphreṁ*, obeisance to the lion-throne of the great jewel of the three worlds (*tribhuvana-mahāratna-siṃhāsana*).

O glorious Śrīmanuśrī Ratnakalaśāmṛta, seated upon the great throne of the Śrīcakrarāja, O Nirvāṇapala Brahmā, O Śrī Guhyakālī: may your life-force remain here, may your vitality remain here; may all your faculties—speech, mind, sight, hearing, taste, and smell—come right here and abide happily for a long time.
Svāhā!

Having thus performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (consecration of the vital breath), one should perform the *mātṛkā-nyāsa*. Having assigned the *ṛṣi*, *chandas*, and so forth of the root mantra, one should assign the *hṛdaya* and other limbs (*aṅga*) to the four corners starting from the southeast (*āgneya*). To the embodiment of the illustrious Ratnakarasamūrti, to Nirvāṇaśrīguhyabhairava, and to the illustrious Guhyakālī, I worship and satiate the illustrious sandals; obeisance! (5) To the supreme nectar, Nirvāṇaśrīguhyakālī, I worship and satiate the illustrious sandals; obeisance!

The venerable *pādukā* (10). The venerable *Siddhilakṣmī*, the venerable *Nirvāṇaśrī*, the venerable *Guhyakālī*, the venerable *pādukā* (10). Thus, having worshipped the Root Goddess (*mūladevī*). (5) The venerable *Kālāgninirvāṇaśrīguhyabhairavī*, the venerable *pādukā* (10). (5) The venerable *Vaṭavānalaguhyabhairavī*, the venerable *pādukā* (10). (5) The venerable *Jvālāmukhīguhyabhairavī*.
The venerable sandals. (10) These [deities] are for the sake of the glorious Śrī-Śakti; they, possessing a golden luster, are to be worshipped in the three corners.

[They hold] a spear, a skull-cup, a vessel for the destruction of sins, a water-pot, a discus, a freshly severed head, a sword, a vessel of nectar, the gesture of knowledge (jñānamudrā), and a vessel of honey.

They should be worshipped in sequence with weapons such as the sword and shield; they sit upon corpses, have fierce and formidable fangs, possess three eyes, and have the moonlight of their matted locks as their crowns.

Standing firm, adorned with skull-tassels, wearing ornaments such as garlands of severed heads, bones, and gems, they are naked, with protruding tongues, terrifying to behold, yet bestowers of desired accomplishments.
Śrī Guhyakālī has emerged from the eyes of the belly, the forehead, and the right eye;
she who is fond of wine, meat, blood, and so forth, is to be worshipped in the five corners in the manner to be described. (5) *Sphreṃ*, together with Bhairava, is the secret of emanation.

*Sphreṃ*, at the time of emanation, the venerable *Śrīpādukā* [of] Guhyakālī together with Guhyabhairava of Emanation; *Sphreṃ*, at the time of maintenance, the venerable *Śrīpādukā* [of] Guhyakālī together with Guhyabhairava of Maintenance; *Sphreṃ*, at the time of withdrawal, the venerable *Śrīpādukā* [of] Guhyakālī together with Guhyabhairava of Withdrawal; *Aphreṃ*, [the venerable *Śrīpādukā* of] Anākhyā Guhyakālī together with Anākhyā Guhyabhairava.
The venerable sandals. (10) (5) Nphreṁ, together with Bhāsāguhyabhairava, O Bhāsāguhyakālī, the venerable sandals. (10) ||
These are the five times; they are to be worshipped in sequence, beginning from the northeast corner.
Just as the powers are concealed by the root deity, so too are these missiles, weapons, and so forth concealed by the root goddess.
And a trident and a vessel for liquor, with hands whose heads and arms have been recently severed.
And [he saw] Kālī,
the supreme goddess who bestows all desires, holding a sword, possessing the aforementioned attire and ornaments, dark-complexioned, and filled with joy.
I bow with Bhairava himself and with Kolaśadvākin.

*Kphreṃ kāli (2) kālacaṇḍayogini sarvasaṃpatpradena mā bhagavati svāhā* || (27) || Thus, preceded by meditation, [one worships] the *śrīpādukā* of Kālī, the sovereign of the glorious five-cornered [maṇḍala]. While protecting [the disciple], one should perform worship: (5) *P(-)hrīṁ*, the venerable sandals of Pūrṇeśvarī together with Pūrṇeśvara;
(10) *Nhrīṁ*, the venerable sandals of Niśeśvarī together with Niśeśvara. (10)

(5) *Sphreṃ*, O Siddheśvara together with Siddheśvarī, [I worship] the venerable *pādukā*. (10)

Thus, these six, seated upon lion-thrones, are to be worshipped with their respective powers (*śakti*). This is their visualization (*dhyāna*).
Dark as a dense blue cloud, standing in the pratyālīḍha posture, possessing three eyes,
adorned with a garland of severed heads and bones, and seated upon a great corpse.
The boon-granting gesture, the gesture of fearlessness, the trident, a skull-cup filled with wine,
a hand-drum, a rosary, a spear, a sugarcane bow, and an arrow.
And holding great swords and discuses, she bears sprout-like hands.
Vāsuki and Śaṅkhapāla serve as her ear-ornaments;
she wears Ananta as a necklace, and is adorned with various other ornaments.
She whose mass of matted hair is tawny and upward-pointing, who has the crescent moon as her crest-ornament,
and who always delights in the sound of the "hā hā" cry within the abode of the Full (Tiruparankuṇram).
In the great and most delightful Mahāpīṭha, at the Lakṣmīvana cremation ground,
she was constantly worshipped by Indra while seated upon the eastern lion-throne.
Terrible with her fangs, she is worshipped by hosts of sages and gods;
she is born from the mouth of Tatpuruṣa and is joined with Pūrṇabhairava.
I bow to Pūrṇeśvarī, the bestower of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Thus ends the meditation on Pūrṇeśvarī.
She whose lotus-face is most terrible, who has appeared with a fearsome luster,
who always resides in the southern cremation ground seated upon a great corpse, wearing a tiger skin as her lower garment and a human skin as her upper garment.
Resembling a mass of lightning and possessing a radiance equal to ten million suns.
Resembling molten gold, with only bones and marrow remaining,
she has five faces, possesses great majesty, and is endowed with fifteen eyes.
The tongue of Mahādaṣṭā is born of power, flickering and terrifying.
I shall make her waist slender with a deep navel, and crown her head with the crescent moon.
With hair flowing upward and loosened, adorned with the king of serpents,
possessing a head-dress along with a skull-ornament,
she is decorated with a garland of heads from which blood still drips from freshly severed necks.
Her sixteen arms are joined with an elephant-hide garment and small bells;
she holds a noose, a goad, a skull-bowl, a khaṭvāṅga staff, a severed head, and a drum.

With her hands she holds a sword, a shield, a noose, an arrow, a bow, a discus, a staff, and a water-pot, as well as the gestures of granting fearlessness, bestowing boons, and the threatening finger.
Frightening the three worlds with the sound of the syllable *huṃ*,
she is the Mistress of the Kula, residing in the heart-lotus of Mahābhairava;
and on the island of Śākapuṣkara, she is the one who beholds the practitioners.
Seated upon the throne in the cavernous abode of the four elements, traversing the path of the yoni-maṇḍala,
she is eternally worshipped by Yama as she is mounted upon his lion-throne.
May sages, gods, asuras, and others worship with faith, devotion, and the like.
I bow to her who grants all desired objects; I prostrate before the one who dwells within the secret depths.
Thus is the meditation on Niśiśvarī.
Now follows the meditation according to the Western Tradition (Paścimāmnāya).
Near the Himavat mountain, she is seated upon a bull,
supreme, with one face, three eyes, and endowed with eighteen arms.
Resembling molten gold, with the crescent moon as his remaining crest-ornament,
he holds a hand-drum, an axe, an arrow, a sword, a goad, and a water-pot.
She holds a conch and a flute in her two excellent right hands;
in her left hands, she bears the gesture of fearlessness, a trident, a bow, a shield,
a skull-cup, a staff, a wine-cup, a bell, and a staff.

I bow to Kubjikā, who is worshipped by the gods, who wears a crown of matted hair that is intensely tawny and upward-pointing, who is endowed with the most beautiful and excellent foliage-like ornaments, who is adorned with breasts like pearls, and who grants all desired objects.
Thus ends the meditation on Kubjikā.
Next is the meditation on the Northern Tradition (Uttarāmnāya).
Dark as a dense blue cloud, she is endowed with nine eyes.
The right face is yellow, while the middle one is dark blue in color.
That face, with its upward-turned mouth resembling a blazing fire, was terrifying and hideous, with a torrent of blood flowing from its mouth;
it was difficult to behold due to its furrowed brows, and its heroic roar was fearsome.
She bears three faces, each with a playfully flickering tongue.
With tawny hair tied in a topknot, she has the crescent moon as her crest-ornament.
She is richly adorned with the beauty of bone ornaments and wears a crown of skulls; she possesses twenty-seven severed heads from which streams of blood flow.
Adorned, bestowing all accomplishments, and possessing the supreme sound of the hero’s bell.
Śivā is mounted upon a corpse, holding a skull-cup filled with blood.
She holds a noose and a khaṭvāṅga staff, as well as a corpse, in her [right] hands;
in her left, she holds a trident, a discus, and a goad.
[One should meditate upon] the maiden who is devoid of qualities (niguṇā), absolute (kevalā), pure (śuddhā), and of the nature of light;
the great-bodied Mahākālī, who has three faces and is Guhyakālikā.
I bow with supreme devotion to the illustrious Uttara Yoginī. One should worship her who has nine faces in this [mantra]. Her meditation [is as follows]:
O Bhairava, upon the severed heads of the guardians of the directions— beginning with Brahmā and ending with Yama, who were like the fires of universal dissolution—
the Goddess Śivā rested upon his upper lip, which was as red as a thousand-petaled lotus.
The Blessed Lady, the supreme one among those with ten faces, is seated upon a lotus;
she whose mouths form a row of lions, elephants, boars, monkeys, bears, horses, Garuḍas, crocodiles, and human beings— she is Yogeśvarī.
[She holds] spears, *kuśa* grass, thunderbolts, mallets, nooses, leaves, skull-topped staffs (*khaṭvāṅga*), and hair-ends, as well as a noose and a lotus.
Thus ends the meditation on the goddess Uttara.
Now follows the meditation on the Ūrdhvāmnāya.
Bhairava [beholds her] seated upon a corpse-lotus, possessing a luster like a ruby,
resembling saffron-water, and radiant with a crown of rubies.
Adorned with various jewels and shining gold,
she holds in her lotus-like hands a noose, a goad, a bow, and arrows.
I bow to Kāmeśvarī, the bestower of the fruits of the four aims of human life.
Thus ends the meditation of the Ūrdhvāmnāya.
Now, the meditation on the unmanifested.
Resembling the fire at the time of universal dissolution, possessing three faces and a certain radiant luster,
her limbs adorned with a garland of severed heads, wearing a sacred thread of passion,
clad in a garment of tiger skin with a lion skin as an upper robe.
Vairocanī is the eastern Vajra, the beloved of the one whose voice is the sound of the Vajra.
Four-armed, seated upon a corpse, with tawny hair tied upward, she holds in her hands a curved knife and a skull-cup, as well as a khaṭvāṅga staff and a hand-drum.

I bow to Vajravairocanī, who wears a garment of intestines, is adorned with golden ornaments, bestows virtue, wealth, and desire, possesses three eyes, bears the moon upon her crest, and desires the sacrificial offering in the cremation ground.
Thus ends the meditation on Vairocana.
